title: Quantized rollout triggered accuracy oscillation and crashloop — follow-ups and mitigations
creator: Sophie Nguyen
description: Summary: During a staged rollout of the new dynamic-int4 hybrid quantization profile (profile-v2), we observed an interplay between kernel selection heuristics and KV cache eviction logic. Symptoms included sudden accuracy oscillations on a small but critical subset of RLHF/long-sequence workloads and a crashloop on a subset of Dedicated nodes caused by repeated operator fallback leading to resource pressure and OOM during prefetch. Immediate action was a rollback of profile-v2 to profile-v1 and scaling down affected Dedicated pools.
timeline:
2025-02-11: profile-v2 rollout began (10% nodes)
2025-02-12 03:12 UTC: first anomaly detected — spike in quant-fallback-rate and kvcache eviction metric for RLHF batch jobs
2025-02-12 03:22 UTC: accuracy regressions reported by internal synthetic eval harness (delta > 7% on safety-critical prompts)
2025-02-12 03:35 UTC: crashloop detected on 4 Dedicated nodes (OOM during prefetch); autoscaler began thrashing
2025-02-12 03:50 UTC: emergency rollback to profile-v1 completed; crashloops stabilized after 17 minutes
2025-02-13: began root-cause analysis and canary coverage review
root_cause: A race condition between the kernel selection path and the new dynamic-int4 fallback decision resulted in a mismatched op-signature assumption for a fused attention operator on a subset of models. That mismatch triggered a software fallback to a slower, memory-intensive kernel. Under our bursty RLHF load (long sequence lengths + KV reuse), the fallback kernel caused repeated KV cache evictions and prefetch storms, which in turn increased memory pressure and led to OOM/crashloop on certain Dedicated nodes. The rollout did not include a sequence-length distribution canary and lacked an op-signature validation gate prior to applying the profile to a node.
impact: Immediate: ~0.6% of production requests saw accuracy swings exceeding our alert threshold; 4 Dedicated nodes crashlooped causing capacity loss and elevated latencies for customers on those pools. Upstream effects: autoscaler instability, elevated token-cost due to fallback to higher-memory kernels. No customer data leaks; no security incident.
action_items: Hotfix: add pre-deploy op-signature validation (sha256 of op schema + shape dims) to the profile applicator — owner: Arjun — ETA 2025-02-18
Add a staged-rollout guardrail that forbids dynamic-int4 profile application to nodes serving seq_len > 2048 without explicit opt-in — owner: Maya Patel (Runtime QA) — ETA 2025-02-25
Create a kvcache eviction alert (kvcache_evictions_per_request > 0.002 for 5m) and connect to on-call runbook — owner: Lina Morales (SRE) — ETA 2025-02-19

Expand canary workloads to include RLHF long-sequence traces (percentile distribution capture and replay) and run nightly synthetic coverage against profile changes — owner: Research Tools — ETA 2025-03-01

Implement a lightweight operator fingerprinting job that records op signatures and kernel compatibility matrix nightly; surface diffs on PRs that touch quant profiles — owner: Connor Wu — ETA 2025-02-28

Improve automatic rollback heuristic: if quant-fallback-rate or accuracy-regression metric crosses threshold during rollout, stop and auto-rollback to previous profile — owner: Platform Controls — ETA 2025-02-26

Document a 'safelist' of fused operators known to be unsupported by dynamic-int4 paths and ensure profile applicator refuses to enable profiling on nodes with those operators — owner: Applied ML — ETA 2025-02-22
Post-incident: run a retrospective with Dedicated customers affected and share impact summary & timeline — owner: Customer Success — ETA 2025-02-27
